_comment: BYS360 coverage ratchet baseline. Truthful, re-measured floor for CI's actual test scope (tests/quality -m "ci_safe" -- unchanged literal marker, now naturally selecting 40 more tests via per-file pytestmark -- then tests/integration tests/architecture tests/security tests/critical tests/services tests/migrations tests/workflow tests/release tests/communication tests/behavior tests/mobile + 32 loose tests/test_*.py files, branch=true). This value is NOT aspirational and must NEVER be raised automatically by any script -- raising it is a separate, human-reviewed action after real coverage genuinely improves. See scripts/quality/bys360_coverage_ratchet.py for enforcement logic and its docstring for the no-self-raise constraint.
_history: Phase 7 Quality/Top-Level CI Coverage Expansion (2026-07-27): 40 tests across 14 tests/quality files that were never marked @pytest.mark.ci_safe (collected but silently deselected from real CI) were brought into scope by adding a module-level pytestmark = pytest.mark.ci_safe to each of the 14 files -- the ci_safe step's own pytest command is UNCHANGED (still the exact literal -m "ci_safe"), because scripts/quality/bys360_quality9_ci_gate.py::check_workflow hard-requires that exact literal value and is outside this expansion's allowed change scope (a marker-expression-widening approach was tried first and rejected after it broke that gate). Separately, 32 of the 33 loose tests/test_*.py files (533 of 536 tests) were added to the broad coverage-instrumented step; tests/test_live_scope_and_security_static.py (3 tests) was deliberately excluded because it carries a module-level pytest.mark.live/realdb/slow despite static-only test bodies -- left for a separate human decision on whether that marker is stale. 573 candidate tests added, plus 136 new contract tests added to the existing tests/architecture/test_ci_coverage_scope_contract.py (already in-scope directory) that lock this expansion in -- 709 tests added to the real count in total; the 136 contract tests are pure JSON/AST/regex parsing of repo config files (0-import, 0% app/ coverage contribution) exactly like the pre-existing contract tests already in that file. 0 cross-scope duplicate node IDs anywhere, 0 skip/xfail beyond the pre-existing 1, stable across 2 isolated runs + 1 full-suite-mixed run + a post-full-suite isolated re-run for every candidate group (quality candidates 40/40, top-level candidates 533/533, combined 573/573, 0 failed every time), and 2 identical final full-scope runs including the new contract tests (1680/1680 passed, 0 failed). Combined coverage measured twice, identically, at 24.138741292664996% -- unchanged to the 15th decimal place before and after the 136 contract tests were added, confirming they contribute 0 measurable app/ coverage as expected. Adds ~14s to the ci_safe step and no measurable net increase to the broad step (395-403s measured across repeated runs vs 409s baseline -- within normal run-to-run variance). Previous baseline (Phase 6 Communication/Behavior/Mobile CI Coverage Expansion, 2026-07-27) was combined_pct=23.45 -- kept in _history for continuity, not reused as the active floor. Earlier baselines: Critical Operational Expansion combined_pct=23.39; CI Coverage Scope Policy Closure (services-only) combined_pct=23.27; Campaign 1B (2026-07-24) combined_pct=18.85 -- see previous_baseline below for the immediately preceding one.

repeatability.note: Two independent full runs of the new combined command (both steps) produced an identical measurement (deterministic given no test randomization is in use): lines 28910/102467, branches 2936/29462 in both runs. The recorded combined_pct is the true measured value, consistent with lines_covered/lines_valid/branches_covered/branches_valid (see tests/quality/test_bys360_coverage_ratchet.py::test_committed_baseline_counts_are_internally_consistent); the sole safety margin is the pre-existing tolerance_pct field below, unchanged at 0.5 points.

tolerance_rationale: Absorbs float rounding and Windows-worktree-vs-Ubuntu-CI-runner platform noise (this baseline was measured on Windows; the actual CI runner is ubuntu-latest, which can take slightly different code paths on OS-conditional branches). Not intended to absorb a real coverage regression, which is expected to be much larger than 0.5 points in practice.
